stills.description: Vasa (or Wasa) is a Swedish warship built between 1626 and 1628. The ship foundered and sank after sailing about 1,300 m (1,400 yd) into her maiden voyage on 10 August 1628. She fell into obscurity after most of her valuable bronze cannons were salvaged in the 17th century until she was located again in the late 1950s in a busy shipping lane just outside the Stockholm harbor. Salvaged with a largely intact hull in 1961, she was housed in a temporary museum called Wasavarvet ("The Wasa Shipyard") until 1988 and then moved to the Vasa Museum in Stockholm. stills.description: The chainwale is the thick plank on the outside of the hull to which the shrouds are fastened. On Vasa, the chainwale is above the gunports of the upper deck. The load of the shrouds is transferred to metal chains which are bolted to the hull below the chainwale. On Vasa, the chainwale's outer edge is angled upwards. On other ships the surface of the chainwale is horizontal, in which case the structure needs substantial bracing to avoid being pushed out of position by the load in the shrouds.
